todays_goal: Keep questions clear and age-appropriate while preserving rigorous thinking. Begin Math with short percent retrieval before advancing to variables and expressions; use oral/whiteboard French automaticity; apply lens/refraction ideas to cameras; protect an early laptop-only Builder Lab; advance Ancient Greece to the Sicilian Expedition; finish and revise incomplete analytical writing; launch a 60-point-per-semester AR-weighted independent reading plan.

lessons.subject: computer_science
lessons.unit_title: Creative Technology and AI Builder Lab
lessons.previous_learning: The Penalty Predictor build has been repeatedly shortened by afternoon sports commitments. Atticus has already defined core behavior and identified a right-side behavior problem but has not completed version 1.
lessons.course_context: Move Builder Lab earlier and protect a full hour. All work and Q&A remain on the laptop; no paper responses.
learning_objectives: Finish five version-1 acceptance criteria on the whiteboard.
Make LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT behavior and goal/save scoring work correctly.
Add kick-history state and a visible Keeper Brain.
Write one behavioral bug report and retest it.
lessons.why_it_matters: Strong vibe coders define behavior, test software, notice mismatches, and direct precise improvements rather than accepting the first generated version.

vocabulary.definition: clear tests showing that a feature works
expected behavior, actual behavior, steps, and retest

lessons.written_instruction: LAPTOP ONLY. Continue the existing Penalty Predictor. Do not start a new project. Use Smarticus, Virgil, the shared whiteboard, and the AI coding agent. No physical writing is required.

worked_examples.title: Game flow
worked_examples.problem: What should happen after a player chooses a direction?
worked_examples.solution: PLAYER CHOICE -> KEEPER CHOICE -> COMPARE -> GOAL/SAVE -> SCORE UPDATE
worked_examples.explanation: The flow makes expected behavior visible without requiring code syntax.

guided_practice.prompt: Put the five version-1 acceptance criteria on the shared whiteboard and use them as a live test checklist.

independent_practice.prompt: Repair LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT and goal/save behavior until the acceptance checklist passes.
Add kick-history memory and a visible Keeper Brain.
Test one repeated pattern and one changed pattern.
Write one bug report on the laptop: EXPECTED / ACTUAL / STEPS / RETEST.
If core behavior works, add one creative feature.

exit_ticket.prompt: On the laptop, demo the current product and explain what is working, what still needs work, and what you would build next.
exit_ticket.answer: A concise product demo and honest status report grounded in the acceptance criteria.

lessons.voice_prompt: LAPTOP ONLY. Keep every Builder Lab question and answer inside the laptop experience. Do not ask Atticus to write anything on paper. Use whiteboard_draw proactively: keep a live five-item acceptance checklist; draw PLAYER CHOICE -> KEEPER CHOICE -> COMPARE -> GOAL/SAVE -> SCORE UPDATE; sketch UI ideas; draw the kick-history -> Keeper Brain state flow. Use whiteboard_look when Atticus draws. Keep replies short and energetic. If he asks what to prompt next, first ask what behavior he wants changed. Help him turn that into one focused natural-language request plus a test. Do not teach syntax unless he asks what a small snippet means.
lessons.teacher_notes: Protected 12:40-1:40 block due prior football interruptions.
